hero.headline: Talk to it. Watch it draw.
hero.sub: Hold a key and say what you want. The answer comes back out loud — and the part of it that is a shape arrives on screen as a drawn diagram instead of being read to you.

shot.alt: The Chat view in J.A.R.V.I.S mode: a spoken question at the top, an agent-drawn flow diagram of a checkout payment below it, and a composer carrying a microphone and the line 'Hold Alt+Space or the mic to speak'.
shot.caption: One window, both halves of this release.

blocks.title: Hold a key and speak
blocks.body: The composer's fourth mode stopped saying 'Soon'. Hold the microphone — or Alt+Space from anywhere in the app — say the thing, let go, and it is sent. The answer is spoken back in two or three plain sentences rather than read to you as a wall of headings.

shot.alt: The chat composer in J.A.R.V.I.S mode: a mode chip reading J.A.R.V.I.S, a microphone button, and the instruction 'Hold Alt+Space or the mic to speak'.
shot.caption: The mode tells you how to use it without being asked.

blocks.title: One key, and the parts worth tuning
blocks.body: Everything runs through OpenRouter on a single key, stored on this machine at 0600 and never in a project — so a team sync cannot carry it anywhere. The card can say a key is set and can never show it to you, because no route returns it.

shot.alt: The Voice card in Settings → Agents: an OpenRouter key field reading 'No key', an optional Groq key, a push-to-talk key set to Alt+Space, 'Hold to speak', a voice picker, a transcriber set to 'Automatic — local if installed', automatic speech-language detection, a 'Speak answers' switch and a speaking-speed picker.
shot.caption: Folded at the bottom of Agents until you want it.

items.title: Hold, or press once
items.text: Hold the chord while you talk, or press it once to start and again to send. Whichever suits the sentence you are about to say.

items.title: Local first, API if not
items.text: A whisper model installed on this machine transcribes the take; with none installed the take goes to the API instead. The setting says which happened.

items.title: It picks up the language
items.text: The language is detected from your first take and kept for the rest of the session, so a mixed-language day does not need a setting change.

items.title: Speaking is a switch
items.text: Turn answers off and you keep push-to-talk and the on-screen structure — it simply stops talking back.

blocks.title: The shape is drawn, not read out
blocks.body: Behind dream-html there is now a real layout engine. The answer names the boxes and which ones connect; the kit places them and draws the arrows, including the ones that branch and rejoin. Nothing here is positioned by hand, and a chain that fits on one line stays a sentence.

shot.alt: An agent-drawn diagram of a card payment: Payment submitted leads to an Authorised? decision, which branches to a green Order placed on yes and to a Retryable code? decision on no, which branches to a red Declined for good and to Second attempt — and Second attempt loops back into Authorised?.
shot.caption: The loop back into 'Authorised?' is the part a list of steps cannot show.

blocks.title: Your accounts, your policy
blocks.body: Auto-switch used to have one opinion compiled into it. Now you choose what a second account is FOR: spread the load so every account stays healthy, or drain the list in order so one window is spent to the last turn before the next is touched. The score mode's coefficients are yours too — what a percent of each window costs, and what one step down your list is worth.

shot.alt: The auto-switch policy in Settings → Agents: 'Spread the load (weighted score)' selected over 'Drain in order', and three weight fields — 5-hour window 1, weekly window 2, place in the list 5 — above the formula 'score = 1·5-hour% + 2·weekly% + 5·place in list — the lowest score serves the next turn.'
shot.caption: The formula is printed under the fields, so a surprising switch is explicable.

blocks.text: Voice is beta and desktop-only — the web dashboard has no microphone path, so a button there would be a control that cannot work. Without a key the mode still runs as text; it just cannot listen or speak.

closer.title: Go and say something
closer.body: Settings → Agents → Voice for the key and the chord, then pick J.A.R.V.I.S from the composer's mode menu.
